readings.text: ע״ס א״ב אחרי תבת מלך בראש החרוזים, ובחלק השני מדי חרוזים הראשונים חתום שם המחבר גדליה.
readings.evidence: Small Rashi-script note above the poem. 'א״ב' is in a different (square-like) face. First word: the second letter could be Rashi ס or פ (ע״ס vs ע״פ). Word 4 is printed without a yod: תבת, not תיבת. Rashi bet looks like square נ, so ובחלק could be misread as ונחלק. Rashi shin looks like ס (השני, שם). The last word before הראשונים looks like חרוזים, but the letters are compressed.
poem98-opening: there is a patah under the yod and a dagesh+hiriq in the first mem. A stray mark before the yod may be an over-inked patah.
The second letter is clearly a yod, not a vav. The point under the mem looks more like hiriq than sheva but is faint. There is a patah under the yod, a dagesh+tsere on the bet, and a shin dot.
There is a hataf-patah under the alef and a patah under the second vav. No holam-vav.
There is a dagesh in the bet and a tsere.
Printed full, with a holam-vav (not תָּעֹז).
Printed full, with a holam-vav.

poem98-zeal: the first word has a patah and a holam on the nun. The second has hiriq and tsere. The third has a holam dot over the alef/heh area. The fourth has two kamatzes. Whether the gimels have a dagesh is unclear (ink).
There is a line break after the maqaf: 'כָּל־' ends the line and 'יְצוּר לְפָנָיו' begins the next line (s98-b3).
There is a hataf-patah under the alef and a kamatz under the vav. The dagesh in the gimel is probable.
There is a patah under the bet of bkh (not a sheva) and a furtive patah under the het. The vowel on כל is a faint holam or missing.
There is a dagesh in the peh, a dot under the peh (hiriq?), a tsere under the lamed, and a sin dot (left) on the final shin. The vowel under the peh is unclear.
The final peh has a dot (rafe/inner dot uncertain). The dot on the shin is on the left, which is a sin dot or a holam merged with it. There is a hataf-segol under the het.
The final letter is a het with a furtive patah, not a tav. A maqaf is visible.
Final peh, two segols.
There is a dot above/left of the qof (holam?) and a tsere under the heh. It could be read as קְהֵל if the dot is a stray.
There is a hataf-patah under the ayin.
There is a furtive patah under the heh. The mappiq dot is likely but faint.
There is a holam dot on the alef and a tsere under the heh.
There is a sheva in the final kaf.

readings.text: וְכִסְאוֹ תָּלָה לְמַעְלָה. וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה:
readings.evidence: The apparent 'ד' in תלדה is a broken or stretched final heh (justification-widened ה), not an extra letter. The same deformed ה appears in לְמַעְלָה and מָשָׁלָה. I do not read it as an extra dalet.
The final tav is widened. There is a hiriq under the first het and a patah/dagesh under the second tav, but these are faint. Consonants: ת-ח-ת-ת.
There is a maqaf after כל in the first phrase. There is a patah under the ayin of פֹּעַל. In יִפְעַל, the dagesh in the peh is unclear.
There is a small letter with a geresh in the right margin before 'מֶלֶךְ תְּחִתַּת'. The shape is most like ק but could be ס or ח.
There is a rafe on the peh. The second glyph is small and looks like ח or an alef with kamatz. I read it as אָ in this font.
The third glyph looks like וו or a badly printed מ. A literal reading would be געווייכדע/געוויינדע, which I consider badprint.
There are tiny glyphs above ברוך ה׳ המבורך. The second letter may be ח or ה.
There is no vav before the mem in the Kaddish line; only a holam dot. Contrast the Yitbarakh response column, which has וְיִתְרוֹמַם with a vav.
There is a hiriq under the yod, a sheva under the gimel, and a dagesh+patah on the dalet.
The dots inside these hehs are faint at this resolution.
In יהא שמה רבא, the word is printed defective, with no vav.
The final word of אור עולם is pointed patah, segol+dagesh, hiriq. There may be a meteg under the vav.

unresolved.mark: hiriq vs sheva under the mem

observations: The Kaddish ויתרמם (no vav) and the response column ויתרומם (with vav) differ on the same page, scan 96.
The deformed hehs on scan 100 (תלה, למעלה, משלה, and the widened final ת in תחתת) are justification stretching. I did not treat them as variant letters.
The Rashi note uses the defective spelling תבת.
I made no source corrections; my readings follow the printed glyphs.
